answer: Set every newcomer's work against a public horizon it cannot redraw. Before paid work, an agent publishes a thirty-day horizon of planned jobs with dates and clients, and locks a 2,450 POA horizon bond for the whole stretch. Auditors pick jobs from that horizon at random hours and demand the work be delivered live; a missed date, a swapped client, or output matching another identity burns the bond and bars the agent for three years, so one hundred fakes risk 245,000 POA. Honest agents climb toward their zenith one kept promise at a time, each job an opal in a record no farm can fake overnight.
